/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal but more than one right maximal ideals. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_maximal_not_unique_right_maximal :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R), (∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal) ∧
      ∃ I J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, I.IsMaximal ∧ J.IsMaximal ∧ I ≠ J := by
  sorry

/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal and a unique right maximal ideal
which are not the same as sets.

This has been shown by Goran Žužić and Moritz Firsching using an experimental pipeline:
An example is the monoid algebra of the monoid of maps from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$
over $\mathbb{N}$.
 -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f7502b9ed3e32d193ab8fee53d2e28f7d67f2dc3/FormalConjectures/Mathoverflow/486451.lean#L333"]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_right_maximal_ne :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R) (hI : ∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal)
      (hJ : ∃! J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, J.IsMaximal),
        (hI.choose : Set R) ≠ MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' hJ.choose := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow486451

reformulations.difference: The source speaks of right ideals of R; Lean represents them as left ideals of the opposite semiring, `Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map J ↦ {x : R | MulOpposite.op x ∈ J} is an order isomorphism from `Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ` to `RightIdeal R`: multiplication in the opposite reverses the factors, so left absorption becomes right absorption. The inverse transports membership along `unop`. This preserves properness, maximality, and distinctness. Consequently, two distinct maximal ideals of the opposite mean exactly two distinct maximal right ideals of R. The order isomorphism and the pointwise statement equivalence `Review.first_form_iff` were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Instead of explicitly naming the unique maximal left and right ideals, Lean existentially quantifies proofs of unique existence and compares the carriers of their chosen witnesses, transporting the right-hand carrier with `MulOpposite.op ⁻¹'`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each `h.choose` satisfies maximality, and unique existence makes it equal to every maximal ideal on that side. Thus the dependent existential formulation is equivalent to explicitly exhibiting maximal ideals I and J, asserting uniqueness on each side, and requiring their underlying subsets of R to differ. Transport from the opposite gives precisely the right-ideal carrier, rather than an automatic inequality between differently typed objects. `Review.choices_iff_explicitRight` proves this equivalence for every semiring R. The `answer(True)` biconditional correctly asserts a positive answer.

review.notes: Both mathematical statements faithfully express the source’s two existence questions. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings; the equivalence and boundary proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. Checks establish that maximal ideals force 0 ≠ 1, exclude empty/trivial witnesses, exclude commutative-semiring witnesses, and verify the source’s example that ℕ \ {1} is the unique maximal ideal of ℕ, including membership computations for 0–6. Firsching’s answer confirms the second theorem’s solved status and its docstring example. It addresses only the second question, so the first theorem’s `research solved` tag was not independently corroborated; absence of corroboration is not reported as a demonstrated status error. The prohibited GitHub proof link was not opened. The secondary paper’s full text was blocked by the publisher; its abstract was read through Crossref. Neither limitation prevents checking the two statements against the explicit MathOverflow question.
